items.title: Anthropic IPO valued at $1.5 trillion in record debut
items.feedTitle: Anthropic begins trading as a $1.5 trillion company in the biggest IPO on record as shares spike
items.summary: AI safety-focused company Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, valuing the firm at $1.5 trillion—the largest initial public offering in US history. Shares opened significantly above the IPO price, signaling strong investor appetite for AI stocks despite recent market uncertainty over Nvidia's leadership transition and concerns about an AI valuation bubble.

items.title: Kushner says Russia comfortable with NATO-like Ukraine guarantees
items.feedTitle: Kushner says Russia is 'comfortable' with NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine to end war after Trump talks with Putin
items.summary: Jared Kushner reported that Russia expressed comfort with NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine as a potential path to ending the war, following Trump's talks with Putin in China. Ukrainian officials and European governments have expressed alarm that Ukraine's fate may be determined by bilateral agreements between Trump and Putin without Kiev's full participation.

items.title: Heavy rain, evacuation warnings hit Southern California
items.feedTitle: Rain ramping up across SoCal with evacuation warnings in place for burn scar areas
items.summary: An El Niño-driven storm system brought heavy rains across Southern California, prompting evacuation warnings in burn scar areas vulnerable to flash flooding. The slow-moving system caused widespread disruption, with authorities expressing concern about mudslides and debris flows in recently burned regions.

items.title: Florida executes 20th inmate, setting new state record
items.feedTitle: As some states move away from the death penalty, Florida prepares to set new record
items.summary: Florida is set to execute its 20th inmate of 2026 on Thursday, establishing a new state record for executions in a single year. The milestone comes as other US states have been moving away from capital punishment, making Florida's trend a stark outlier.

items.title: Democrats nominate Katherine Clark as House majority leader
items.feedTitle: Incoming House majority leader Katherine Clark stresses Democratic unity
items.summary: House Democrats nominated Katherine Clark of Massachusetts as the next House majority leader, marking a historic first for a woman in the role. The nomination positions Clark to lead the Democratic majority when the party takes control of the House in January.

stlouis.title: MetroLink extension to airport opens November 30
stlouis.feedTitle: MetroLink extension to MidAmerica St. Louis Airport gets opening date
stlouis.summary: St. Louis's MetroLink light rail expansion to MidAmerica Airport is set to begin service on November 30, following the Thanksgiving holiday. The extension marks a significant infrastructure milestone for the region, improving connectivity between downtown and the airport.

stlouis.title: St. Louis doctors warn over measles elimination loss
stlouis.feedTitle: St. Louis doctors sound alarm after US loses measles elimination status
stlouis.summary: Physicians in the St. Louis area have sounded alarm after the United States lost its measles elimination status, citing resurgence risks in the region. The development comes amid broader concerns about vaccine coverage and disease surveillance gaps.

stlouis.title: Thousands lose St. Louis County tax credit
stlouis.feedTitle: Thousands lose St. Louis County tax credit
stlouis.summary: Thousands of St. Louis County residents have lost access to a local tax credit, impacting their financial circumstances. Details on the cause and scope of the credit loss remain limited from available reporting.

items.feedTitle: Putin says Russia won't negotiate limited ceasefire with Ukraine after bridge strike
items.summary: Summary unavailable for this update.

items.title: Houthis strike Saudi Arabia's tallest skyscraper
items.feedTitle: Iran-backed Houthi 'terrorist attack' hits Riyadh's tallest skyscraper and HQ of Saudi Public Investment Fund
items.summary: Iran-backed Houthi forces launched a missile attack that damaged Riyadh's PIF Tower, the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund. The strike represents an escalation in regional tensions and adds to growing concerns about Middle East instability amid broader US-Iran tensions.

items.title: Trump, Xi, Putin hold unprecedented trilateral summit
items.feedTitle: Trump, Putin and Xi release 'peace declaration' after historic meeting
items.summary: President Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping, and Russian President Putin met for the first trilateral summit of the three powers in Shenzhen, China. They issued a joint 'peace declaration' but made no concrete progress on the Ukraine or Iran conflicts, with analysts describing the meeting as more spectacle than substance.

items.title: UK, EU plan talks on third-country asylum hubs
items.feedTitle: UK and EU plan first talks on sending refused asylum seekers to third countries
items.summary: The UK and EU are preparing formal talks about sending rejected asylum seekers to third-country processing hubs as part of a broader reset agreement. A leaked document indicates both sides plan to commit to discussing the contentious proposal, which follows a five-country Rwanda deal.

items.title: Ukraine strikes Crimean Bridge for third time weekly
items.feedTitle: Ukraine strikes Putin’s prized Crimean bridge for third time in a week
items.summary: Ukraine attacked Russia's prized Kerch Bridge crossing from Crimea to mainland Russia for the third time in a week, inflicting significant damage. Putin vowed a 'painful' retaliation, escalating the conflict as Ukraine maintains pressure on Russian military infrastructure.

items.title: India, Japan deepen defense cooperation, flag economic coercion
items.feedTitle: India, Japan flag 'economic coercion'; agree to deepen strategic, defence cooperation at Tokyo meet
items.summary: India and Japan agreed to strengthen strategic and defense ties during high-level talks, including a historic first allowing Japanese forces to use Indian missile ranges for live-firing exercises. Both nations also flagged concerns about economic coercion by larger trading partners.

items.title: India's Muslim population share to rise by 2070, study finds
items.feedTitle: India’s Hindu and Muslim populations will grow by 2070, but only Muslims’ share will rise. Here’s why
items.summary: A Pew Research report projects that while both Hindu and Muslim populations in India will grow in absolute numbers by 2070, the Muslim share of India's total population will increase while the Hindu share declines. The study attributes the shift to differences in fertility rates between communities.

items.title: PM Modi questions India Inc on jobs and wages amid tax cuts
items.feedTitle: Tax cuts given, but where are jobs, higher wages? PM Modi asks India Inc
items.summary: Prime Minister Modi criticized Indian industrialists for failing to create jobs and raise wages despite receiving significant tax cuts from his government. His remarks reflected frustration over the gap between corporate profit gains and wage growth for workers.

items.title: Rahul Gandhi rules out poll boycott, calls democracy sacred
items.feedTitle: Boycotting polls will end democracy, says Rahul Gandhi; calls Indian democracy ‘sacred’
items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi rejected calls to boycott elections, stating that abandoning the electoral process would end Indian democracy. He characterized India's democratic system as 'sacred' while continuing to critique governance and economic management.

items.title: Congress veteran alleges own party stalled Modi probe
items.feedTitle: ‘Next would have been Modi’: Veerappa Moily alleges Congress leaders stalled probe during UPA rule
items.summary: Senior Congress figure Veerappa Moily alleged that Congress leaders deliberately stalled an investigation into Prime Minister Modi during the UPA government, claiming that proceeding would have targeted Modi. The claim has sparked internal party controversy.

immigration.title: DOL proposes sweeping overhaul to PERM green card process
immigration.feedTitle: Modernizing the Labor Market Test and Improving Protections for U.S. Workers in the PERM Immigrant Visa Program
immigration.summary: The US Department of Labor has proposed major changes to the PERM labor certification program for permanent green cards, with rules tightening recruitment standards and removing expedited pathways for certain categories like nurses and physical therapists. The proposal, not yet finalized, aims to prioritize American workers and strengthen labor market testing requirements.

immigration.title: Texas governor-elect vows to reverse H-1B visa freeze
immigration.feedTitle: Hinojosa Plans to Reverse H-1B Visa Freeze at Public Universities
immigration.summary: Incoming Texas Governor Gina Hinojosa pledged to roll back the state's freeze on hiring H-1B visa holders, which was imposed under outgoing Governor Greg Abbott. Her proposed policy reversal signals a shift in state-level immigration stance affecting skilled worker recruitment.

immigration.title: US reportedly plans largest mass visa revocation in history
immigration.feedTitle: U.S. set for largest mass visa revocation in history targeting up to 200,000 foreigners, officials say
immigration.summary: According to reports, the US State Department is preparing to revoke as many as 200,000 visas in what could be the largest mass visa cancellation in American history. The action reportedly targets specific visa categories, though details on the scope and timing remain limited.

items.title: TSMC tightens China AI chip curbs as new US rules close loophole
items.feedTitle: TSMC tightens China AI chip curbs as new US rules close manufacturing loophole, sources say
items.summary: Taiwan's TSMC is tightening restrictions on AI chip sales to China in response to new US regulations that close a manufacturing loophole. The move reflects intensifying US-China technology competition and efforts to restrict Beijing's access to advanced semiconductors.

items.title: JPMorgan Chase reports cyberattack on third-party vendors
items.feedTitle: Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Customer Data Leaked by Hackers
items.summary: JPMorgan Chase disclosed that third-party vendors providing services to the financial giant were targeted in a cyberattack, potentially exposing some customer data. The breach adds to a mounting wave of financial sector cybersecurity incidents.

items.title: Iran war creates biggest-ever global oil trade disruption, IEA warns
items.feedTitle: There is no going back ‘to the way it was before’ the Iran war’s energy shock, IEA says
items.summary: The International Energy Agency warns that the Iran conflict has triggered the largest disruption to global oil trade in history, with no return to pre-war conditions. Oil markets face structural challenges as regional tensions persist and supply chains remain stressed.

items.title: Walmart raises outlook as wealthy shoppers hunt for deals
items.feedTitle: Walmart Raises Outlook as Wealthier Shoppers Hunt for Deals
items.summary: Walmart raised its full-year outlook as the retailer reported strong sales momentum, with wealthier shoppers increasingly shopping its stores for value amid higher living costs. The company's digital sales now drive growth more than physical stores.

finance.note: Oil prices steadied Thursday after earlier gains on Iran tensions and US inventory concerns, while equities declined broadly despite Anthropic's record-breaking IPO debut—the $2 trillion valuation failed to reignite the broader AI rally. The Fed's hawkish messaging on interest rates (amid AI demand inflation concerns) weighed on sentiment; watch for trade policy clarity from Trump-China talks and whether the Anthropic debut signals sustained institutional appetite for mega-cap AI valuations or a warning sign of froth.

cards.title: Sleep debt doesn't vanish on weekends
cards.insight: Many people assume weekend catch-up sleep erases the harm of chronic sleep deprivation. Research shows sleep debt accumulated during the week damages metabolism, immune function, and mood regulation—and a Saturday night binge cannot fully reverse the cumulative cost.
cards.takeaway: Prioritize consistent weekday sleep over 7+ hours nightly; view weekend sleep as maintenance, not recovery from chronic deficit.

cards.title: Stress amplifies perception of pain
cards.insight: The nervous system in a prolonged stress state lowers pain thresholds and increases sensitivity to discomfort. Chronic anxiety and work pressure don't just feel bad; they rewire how your brain processes physical sensation, turning minor aches into major ones.
cards.takeaway: When pain flares without clear injury, assess stress levels first; calming techniques (breathing, movement, nature) may reduce pain faster than medication.

cards.title: Movement is cognitive medicine
cards.insight: Exercise—especially moderate-intensity activity like brisk walking—releases neurotransmitters that improve focus, mood, and memory more reliably than many pharmaceutical interventions. Even short bursts improve mental clarity for hours after.
cards.takeaway: Before reaching for caffeine or stimulants, take a 15-minute walk or do light strength work to sharpen focus and stabilize mood naturally.

cards.title: Social isolation harms immunity as much as poor diet
cards.insight: Loneliness activates the same chronic inflammatory pathways that poor nutrition does, weakening immunity and increasing susceptibility to infection and illness. Remote work and digital life can mask deeper connection deficit.
cards.takeaway: Schedule in-person time with others weekly—even brief, low-stakes contact (coffee, group fitness) counters inflammation and strengthens resilience.

ai.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon AI model for lower costs
ai.feedTitle: Google introduces new Gemini 4 AI model Neon
ai.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Neon, a new AI model designed to offer lower costs and improved performance for coding and analysis tasks. The release positions Google to compete in the market for efficient, accessible AI tools beyond the flagship Gemini models.

ai.title: Nvidia stops shipping Hopper AI chips to China
ai.feedTitle: NVIDIA stops shipping licensed Hopper AI chips, including H200, to China
ai.summary: Nvidia announced it has ceased shipping licensed Hopper AI chips, including the H200 variant, to China in compliance with US export control regulations. The move reflects ongoing US efforts to restrict Beijing's access to advanced semiconductor technology amid tech competition concerns.

ai.title: Trump suggests US may allow Nvidia chip sales to China
ai.feedTitle: Trump says U.S. might allow Nvidia AI chip sales to China in two to three years
ai.summary: President Trump said the US might permit Nvidia to sell advanced AI chips to China within two to three years, signaling potential flexibility on current export restrictions. The comment contrasts with existing US policy aimed at limiting Beijing's access to cutting-edge semiconductors.

ai.title: California Governor pitches AI kill-switch regulation
ai.feedTitle: Newsom touts an AI kill switch to halt dangerous OpenAI, Anthropic releases
ai.summary: California Governor Newsom proposed new legislation creating an AI 'kill switch' to halt dangerous AI releases by companies like OpenAI and Anthropic. The proposed regulation would give authorities power to pause AI system deployments deemed to pose imminent risks.
